mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative 20-day forward returns because it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces risk appetite and equity valuations. This relationship is linear and active at all times.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between high and low FEDFUNDS quintiles is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals an active monetary tightening cycle that reduces equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% are not significantly negative compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of a rising federal funds rate (indicating active tightening) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 200) signals a monetary tightening cycle that reduces equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on FEDFUNDS, CPIAUCSL, and their interaction term, or the rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1400) signals an impending economic slowdown that leads to monetary easing, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where HOUST < 1400 are not significantly positive compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A falling industrial production index (INDPRO) is associated with negative 20-day forward returns because it signals a weakening economy that reduces corporate earnings and risk appetite.
failure_condition: The rank correlation between INDPRO and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the t-test for the mean return difference between high and low INDPRO quintiles is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment is rising (UNRATE increasing by >0.2 percentage points in 3 months) and employment is falling (PAYEMS decreasing by >100,000 in 3 months), it signals a deteriorating labor market that leads to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rising > 0.2pp in 3 months and PAYEMS falling > 100k in 3 months
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on UNRATE, PAYEMS, and their interaction term, or the rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high retail sales (RSAFS > 360000), the economy is strong, leading to positive 20-day forward returns as corporate earnings are supported.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where RSAFS > 360000 are not significantly positive compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 (the 2017 base), it signals a recessionary condition that leads to negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where INDPRO < 100 are not significantly negative compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC is below 0.03.
